title: GPT-5.6 Pro Finds Explicit Counterexample Disproving the Dinitz–Garg–Goemans Conjecture
whyItMatters: From a single public ChatGPT prompt, GPT-5.6 Pro constructed a finite network counterexample refuting the 27-year-old Dinitz–Garg–Goemans unsplittable-flow conjecture.
summary: Independent researcher Dmitry Rybin posted a public ChatGPT session on X showing OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Pro disproving the 1999 Dinitz–Garg–Goemans conjecture in combinatorial optimization. The model constructed an explicit small directed network admitting a fractional flow of cost 58 while every unsplittable flow respecting the conjectured capacity-violation bound (≤ 15) has cost at least 60—demonstrating that an off-the-shelf frontier reasoning model could refute a 27-year-old network-flow conjecture on demand.
technicalHighlights: Exhibits an explicit finite directed network where a fractional routing achieves cost 58, yet no unsplittable flow within the Dinitz–Garg–Goemans capacity violation bound (≤ 15) achieves cost below 60.
Refutes a 27-year-old (1999) open conjecture on the cost–congestion trade-off of single-source unsplittable flows.
Produced transparently in a publicly shared ChatGPT session link, making both the AI provenance and the finite counterexample immediately reproducible.
caveats: Released directly via X and a public ChatGPT share link (covered in science press) rather than a refereed journal paper or formal Lean artifact; while the finite graph counterexample is directly verifiable by elementary flow arithmetic, formal archival publication is pending.

scoreRationale.foundational: Cleanly refutes a 27-year-old open conjecture in combinatorial optimization and network routing theory.
scoreRationale.ripple: Striking public proof-of-concept that consumer-accessible reasoning models can refute decades-old research conjectures from a single prompt.
scoreRationale.verification: Finite graph counterexample is directly checkable by exact linear/integer programming arithmetic, though unrefereed and posted on X rather than a journal.
scoreRationale.velocity: Generated an explicit counterexample to a 1999 conjecture in a single interactive ChatGPT session.
